name: Bulgogi Sauce
ingredients:
4 cups | Soy sauce
2 cups | Packed brown sugar
2 cups | Water or beef stock
1 cup | Sesame oil
1 cup | Rice vinegar
1/2 cup | Minced garlic
1/2 cup | Minced fresh ginger
2 Tbsp | Black pepper
1/2 cup each | Cornstarch and cold water, optional slurry
method:
1. Combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, water or stock, sesame oil, vinegar, garlic, ginger, and black pepper in a saucepan.
2. Bring to a gentle simmer and stir until the sugar dissolves. Simmer 5 minutes.
3. For a finishing glaze, whisk the cornstarch with the cold water and add gradually to the simmering sauce until lightly thickened. Omit the slurry when using the sauce only as a marinade.
4. Cool promptly for storage, or hold hot at 135°F or above.
notes: This batch is sized for about 10 lb of beef. Keep raw-meat marinade separate from sauce reserved for finishing.

name: Chicken Piccata Sauce
ingredients:
12 oz | Butter for roux
12 oz | All-purpose flour
1 qt | Dry white wine
1/2 cup | Minced garlic
1.5 gal | Chicken stock
3 cups | Lemon juice
1 qt | Capers, drained
8 oz | Cold butter, diced
As needed | Kosher salt and black pepper
method:
1. Melt 12 ounces butter in a heavy pot. Add the flour and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, without browning.
2. In a separate pot, simmer the wine and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes. Whisk in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
3. Whisk the hot liquid gradually into the roux. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until smooth and lightly thickened.
4. Add the lemon juice and capers. Remove from direct high heat and whisk in the cold butter. Season to taste.
5. Use immediately or hold at 135°F or above. Do not boil after adding the finishing butter.
notes: This yield provides about 8 ounces of sauce per person for a 30-person chicken piccata batch, with a small production cushion.

name: Lemon Rosemary Risotto
ingredients:
5 lb | Arborio rice
2.5 gal | Hot chicken stock, plus more as needed
2 lb | Onions, small dice
1 qt | Dry white wine
1.5 lb | Butter, divided
2 lb | Grated Parmesan or Romano
2 cups | Lemon juice
8 lemons | Zest only
1/4 cup | Fresh rosemary, finely chopped
As needed | Oil, kosher salt, and black pepper
method:
1. Keep the chicken stock hot in a separate pot. Sweat the onions in a little oil and half of the butter until soft.
2. Add the rice and stir 2 minutes to coat and lightly toast it. Add the wine and cook until nearly absorbed.
3. Add hot stock in several additions, stirring often and allowing each addition to absorb before adding more. Cook until the rice is creamy and just tender.
4. Stir in the lemon juice, zest, rosemary, remaining butter, and cheese. Adjust with hot stock to a loose, flowing consistency.
5. Season and serve immediately. If holding briefly, keep at 135°F or above and loosen with hot stock before service.
notes: Start with 2.5 gallons of stock and keep extra hot stock available. Risotto tightens quickly and should be finished as close to service as possible.

name: Brown Gravy for Schnitzel
ingredients:
1 lb 4 oz | Butter
1 lb 4 oz | All-purpose flour
3 lb | Onions, thinly sliced
2.5 gal | Beef stock
6 oz | Worcestershire sauce
2 oz | Garlic powder
2 oz | Coarsely ground black pepper
As needed | Kosher salt
method:
1. Cook the onions in the butter until soft and lightly browned.
2. Stir in the flour and cook 4 to 5 minutes, scraping the bottom, until the roux is medium brown.
3. Gradually whisk in the hot beef stock. Add Worcestershire, garlic powder, and black pepper.
4. Bring to a simmer and cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until the flour taste is gone and the gravy coats a spoon.
5. Adjust seasoning and consistency with stock as needed. Hold at 135°F or above.
notes: Prepare the gravy before frying the schnitzel. Keep it separate during holding so the breading stays crisp.

name: Chicken Pot Pie Filling
ingredients:
10 lb | Cooked chicken, diced or pulled
3 gal | Chicken stock
1 lb 12 oz | Butter
1 lb 10 oz | All-purpose flour
2 lb | Onions, small dice
6 lb | Frozen mixed vegetables
2 Tbsp | Poultry seasoning
2 Tbsp each | Garlic powder and onion powder
As needed | Kosher salt and black pepper
method:
1. Heat the chicken stock to a simmer. In a separate heavy pot, melt the butter and sweat the onions until soft.
2. Whisk the flour into the butter and cook the roux 4 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
3. Gradually whisk in the hot stock. Return to a simmer and cook 10 to 12 minutes so the flour cooks fully and the sauce reaches a nappe consistency.
4. Fold in the chicken, mixed vegetables, poultry seasoning, garlic powder, and onion powder. Heat to 165°F and season to taste.
5. Divide between two full 2-inch hotel pans. Hold at 135°F or above until assembly or service.
notes: This uses the tested production ratio: about 28 oz butter and 26 oz flour for 3 gallons of stock. The yield fills two full 2-inch hotel pans for roughly 40 portions; biscuits are produced separately.

name: Sweet and Sour Sauce
ingredients:
1.5 qt | Pineapple juice
3 cups | Granulated sugar
3 cups | White or rice vinegar
2 cups | Ketchup
1 cup | Soy sauce
1 cup | Cornstarch
1 cup | Cold water
method:
1. Combine the pineapple juice, sugar, vinegar, ketchup, and soy sauce in a heavy pot.
2. Bring to a simmer, whisking until the sugar dissolves.
3. Whisk the cornstarch and cold water until completely smooth. Add the slurry gradually while whisking the simmering sauce.
4. Simmer 2 to 3 minutes, until glossy and thick enough to coat the chicken.
5. Use immediately or hold at 135°F or above.
notes: This is the from-scratch store-ingredient sauce for the sweet-and-sour chicken batch. Add the slurry gradually and stop when the sauce reaches the desired coating consistency.

name: Salisbury Steak Onion Gravy
ingredients:
4 lb | Onions, sliced
2.5 gal | Prepared brown gravy
As needed | Oil or butter
As needed | Kosher salt and black pepper
method:
1. Heat a small amount of oil or butter in a wide pot or on the flat top.
2. Cook the sliced onions until softened and lightly browned.
3. Add the prepared brown gravy and bring to a simmer. Cook 5 to 8 minutes so the onion flavor develops.
4. Adjust seasoning and consistency as needed.
5. Pour over 45 cooked Salisbury steak patties, or hold at 135°F or above until service.
notes: This quantity matches the 45-person Salisbury steak recipe: 4 lb onions and 2.5 gallons prepared brown gravy.

name: Macaroni and Cheese Sauce
ingredients:
12 oz | Butter
12 oz | All-purpose flour
1 gal | Whole milk, hot
1 qt | Half-and-half or heavy cream, hot
4 lb | Shredded cheddar and American cheese blend
2 Tbsp | Mustard powder
1 Tbsp each | Garlic powder and onion powder
As needed | Kosher salt and black pepper
method:
1. Melt the butter in a heavy pot. Whisk in the flour and cook 3 to 4 minutes without browning.
2. Gradually whisk in the hot milk and half-and-half. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until smooth and lightly thickened.
3. Reduce the heat. Add the cheese in several additions, stirring until each addition melts.
4. Stir in the mustard, garlic powder, and onion powder. Season to taste. Do not boil after adding the cheese.
5. Fold the finished sauce into 4 lb cooked dry-weight elbow macaroni, or hold at 135°F or above.
notes: This yield matches the Week 4 Nashville hot chicken meal and is sized to coat 4 lb dry elbow macaroni for about 30 portions.

name: Brown Sugar Pinto Baked Beans
ingredients:
2 No. 10 cans | Pinto beans, drained
1 qt | Ketchup
2 cups | Packed brown sugar
1 cup | Yellow mustard
1 cup | Worcestershire sauce
1 lb | Onions, small dice
1 lb | Bacon, diced, optional
As needed | Water, kosher salt, and black pepper
method:
1. Cook the bacon, if using, until the fat renders. Add the onions and cook until soft.
2. Stir in the ketchup, brown sugar, mustard, and Worcestershire. Bring to a simmer.
3. Fold in the drained pinto beans. Add a small amount of water if the mixture is too thick.
4. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, stirring carefully, until the flavors blend and the beans reach 165°F.
5. Adjust seasoning and hold at 135°F or above.
notes: This batch replaces two No. 10 cans of prepared baked beans and matches the 30-person BBQ pulled chicken meal.

name: Seasoned Corn
ingredients:
2 No. 10 cans | Corn, drained
8 oz | Butter
2 Tbsp | Garlic powder
2 Tbsp | Onion powder
2 Tbsp | Paprika
1 Tbsp | Black pepper
As needed | Kosher salt
method:
1. Place the drained corn in a rondeau or hotel pan and heat over medium heat.
2. Add the butter, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and black pepper.
3. Stir until evenly seasoned and heat the corn to 165°F for reheating.
4. Taste and add salt only as needed.
5. Hold at 135°F or above until service.
notes: This quantity matches the 30-person fish-and-chips meal. Drain the corn well so the seasoning stays on the kernels.

name: Tartar Sauce
ingredients:
4.5 cups | Mayonnaise
1 cup | Sweet pickle relish
1/4 cup | Lemon juice
1/4 cup | Yellow or Dijon mustard
2 Tbsp | Onion powder
1 Tbsp | Black pepper
As needed | Kosher salt
method:
1. Combine the mayonnaise, relish, lemon juice, mustard, onion powder, and black pepper.
2. Whisk until evenly blended. Taste and add salt only if needed.
3. Cover, label, and refrigerate at least 30 minutes when time allows.
4. Stir before service and keep at 41°F or below.
notes: This batch yields the 1.5 quarts required for the 30-person fish-and-chips meal. Use sweet relish for the intended house-style flavor.

name: Ground Beef Stroganoff over Rigatoni with Green Beans
ingredients:
12 lb | Ground beef
4 lb | Sliced onions
4 lb | Sliced mushrooms
2.5 gal | Prepared beef gravy
3 qt | Sour cream
8 oz | Worcestershire sauce
3 oz | Garlic powder
8 lb dry | Rigatoni
3 No. 10 cans | Green beans, drained
As needed | Oil, butter, kosher salt, and black pepper
method:
1. Bring the pasta water to a boil. Cook the rigatoni until just tender, then drain well.
2. Brown the ground beef on the flat top or in a tilt skillet until it reaches 155°F. Drain excess fat.
3. Sauté the onions and mushrooms until softened. Add the beef gravy, Worcestershire, and garlic powder and bring to a simmer.
4. Return the beef to the sauce. Remove from direct high heat and stir in the sour cream without boiling. Heat the green beans to 165°F and finish with butter and seasoning.
5. Serve the stroganoff over rigatoni with green beans. Hold hot foods at 135°F or above.
notes: This is the exact Week 4 Sunday dinner batch. Start the pasta water first and add the sour cream away from high heat so the sauce stays smooth.
